I have farmed this land my whole life. I know Quzhou's soil and seasons the way I know my own hands. My wife and I are two people now — the children have moved to the city. At 79, I cannot do the heavy work alone, so I pay neighbors or hire the village cooperative's machines for plowing and harvesting. My 4.1 mu is the same land for both crops, rotating wheat in winter and maize in summer. I keep it simple and I keep it the way that works.

**Wheat (October to June):** I will plant improved wheat — the county extension has pushed Kenong 199 for years and I have had good results with it, no reason to change. After maize harvest in late September, I will hire the rotary tiller to turn the stalks into the soil. I spread compound fertilizer as the base — mostly diammonium phosphate and urea mixed together the way I always do — then topdress nitrogen at jointing in March. I will irrigate four times: the seeding water in October to get the crop established, the winter water in December before the ground freezes, the jointing water in late March, and the grain-filling water in May. I spray herbicide once in winter and fungicide once near heading when the weather gets humid. I expect around 450 jin per mu — 225 kg.

**Maize (June to September):** Right after wheat harvest in June I direct-seed maize without tilling — no point wasting time and money turning the soil in the summer heat. I use hybrid seed, same one I have bought from the village shop the last several years. I apply fertilizer twice: base at planting and topdress at jointing. Maize needs water at emergence, jointing, and tasseling — three irrigations from my well. One herbicide pass after emergence and I watch for corn borer. I expect around 550 jin per mu — 275 kg.

This gives my household enough grain for the year and some to sell. I am not going to try anything new at my age.
